newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin meets Chubais on address, summit.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin meets Chubais on address, summit.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin met his chief-of staff Anatoly Chubais on Friday to discuss his annual address to parliament, which will probabaly take place on March 6, Kremlin spokesman Sergei Yastrzhembsky said.
Yegor Stroyev, the head of the upper house of parliament, had said on Thursday that the address was likely on March 5.

Yastrzhembsky said Yeltsin and Chubais also discussed next month's summit between Yeltsin and U.S. President Bill Clinton and the hostage crisis in Tajikistan, where rebels are holding Russian journalists and U.N. military observers.

Outlining Yeltsin's plans for the coming week, Yastrzhembsky said the president would meet Defence Minister Igor Rodionov on Monday, Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat on Tuesday and U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Friday.
All meetings would take place in the Kremlin, Yastrzhembsky said.

Yeltsin, 66, has held several meetings in the Kremlin since he was released from hospital in January after treatment for pneumonia. Aides said on Wednesday he needed at least another 10 days to recover fully from the illness, which struck as Yeltsin was recovering from open heart surgery.
Yastrzhembsky also said Yeltsin would meet senior European Union officials in Moscow on March 3.
